_note: Evergreen editorial seed pool for the-libertine, written by Claude on 2026-11-05 for owner review. Tips, ideas, real tools (homepage links only) and generic opportunities. No news: news only comes from the brand's listed feeds. Edit freely.

items.title: Spend one evening a week without a screen
items.summary: Freedom starts with where your attention goes.

items.title: Host a dinner where the only rule is no small talk
items.summary: Ask a real question and let it run.

items.title: Write the opposite of your opinion as fairly as you can
items.summary: If you cannot state the other side so its holders agree, you do not understand it yet.

items.title: Read one primary text instead of three summaries
items.summary: Original voices surprise you in ways summaries cannot.

items.title: Keep a question list, not just a to-do list
items.summary: Questions you carry around get answered in unexpected places.

items.title: Start a one-chapter reading group
items.summary: Small enough to finish, deep enough to argue about.

items.title: Hold a debate where each side argues the position they reject
items.summary: It is the fastest way to find the weak spots in your own view.

items.title: Write a letter to a thinker who disagrees with you
items.summary: You do not have to send it. Writing it clarifies what you actually believe.

items.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
items.summary: Free, peer-reviewed articles on philosophical topics.

items.title: Project Gutenberg
items.summary: Free ebooks of classic works whose copyright has expired.

items.title: Internet Archive
items.summary: A free library of books, recordings and web history.

items.title: Audit a free philosophy or history course
items.summary: Many universities publish full courses at no cost.

items.title: Join or start a philosophy café
items.summary: Cafés and libraries often host open discussion nights.

items.title: Look at one artwork for ten full minutes
items.summary: Past the first reaction, a picture keeps giving.

items.title: Visit a gallery on its quiet day
items.summary: You can stand where you like and look as long as you like.

items.title: Start a small collection of postcards or prints
items.summary: Cheap, personal and a good reason to visit museum shops.

items.title: Trade a drawing a week with a friend
items.summary: A low-pressure habit that adds up.

items.title: Google Arts & Culture
items.summary: Explore artworks and exhibitions from museums around the world.

items.title: Europeana
items.summary: Millions of digitized artworks, books and recordings from European institutions.

items.title: Volunteer at a gallery or arts festival
items.summary: Volunteers see behind the scenes and often get free entry.
